∗Heavy gases in the atmosphere descend whereas lighter gases are found in the upper layers as they ascend. As a result CO₂ gases extend up to 20 km from the surface, oxygen, and nitrogen up to 100 km, hydrogen up to 125 km and other gases rise far above 125 km except ozone. The atmosphere is made up of different layers of gases with varying densities and temperatures. Based on these factors different layers of the atmosphere are as follows-

(1) Troposphere – The lowest layer of the atmosphere is called troposphere. All weather activities like clouds, hail, fog, blizzards, thunder, windstorms, etc. are confined to the troposphere. The most important characteristic of the troposphere is that there is a decrease of 6.5° C with an increase of every 1000 min altitude. This decrease in temperature with an increase in altitude is known as normal lapse rate. The upper boundary of the troposphere is called tropopause.

(2) Stratosphere – Stratosphere (15-50 km) is the second most important layer of the atmosphere. It lies between mesosphere (above) and troposphere (below). This layer of atmosphere is very dry in nature and has the least amount of water vapor in it. As a result, there is no weather activity in stratosphere. The stratosphere is used for aviation purposes as the absence of weather activities makes this layer ideal for flying. Ozone layer is found in this sphere.

(3) Mesosphere – This layer is found at an altitude of 50 to 80 km. The upper ceiling of mesosphere is called mesopause.

  • (4) Ionosphere – It is an electrically conducting layer, that makes radio wave transmission possible over long distances. Ionosphere extends from 80 to 640 km.
  • The unique feature of Ionosphere is the phenomenon of Aurora Borealis in Northern Hemisphere and Aurora Australis in Southern Hemisphere.

(5) Exosphere – It is the topmost layer of the atmosphere and is situated above the ionosphere. This layer has no defined boundary. The Communication satellites are positioned in the exosphere.

Dust is higher in subtropical and temperate areas than equatorial and polar ones because dry winds are more common there; so Statement II is false.

Chapter 144

The Insolation

12 facts · 1 Must know

Test mode is on: tap a grey box to reveal the answer.

Key facts from the book (7 points)

∗The only source of energy for the Earth’s atmosphere and its surface is the Sun. The outer layer of the Sun i.e. the photosphere releases energy at a constant rate. As a result, each per unit area of the Earth also receives constant solar energy. This phenomenon is known as the solar constant. ∗ Distribution of Solar Energy – Normally the solar energy received decreases from the equator towards poles. However, there are temporal changes in the energy received at every latitude. Since the Sun’s position in comparison to that of the Earth shifts northwards and southwards during Earth’s revolution due to Earth's tilta the maximum solar energy received also shifts north and south of the equator in the same respect. 20° North Latitude receives the maximum solar energy not the equator.

∗Regions where the Sun’s rays fall in a slanted manner receive less solar energy compared to regions where the Sun’s rays are falling vertically.

∗Albedo is the measure of how much light that hits a surface is reflected without being absorbed. Earth has an average albedo of 30% whereas the maximum albedo effect is produced by surfaces such as glaciers and snow (75-95%). Deserts have an albedo of 20-30%, paddy fields 3-15% and prairies 10-20%.

  • ∗Water vapors are capable ofabsorbing the infrared radiation waves and the outgoing long waves of the dispersed solar waves however, water vapors are transparent to the ultraviolet rays of the sun, hence are incapable ofabsorbing them.
  • On clouded nights the amount of water vapours in the atmosphere is greater compared to a clear sky night. The outgoing long waves are absorbed by the water vapours present in the atmosphere. Hence, cloudy nights are warmer than clear sky nights.

∗Heat Budget-Energy Balance – the rays of the Sun enter the Earth’s atmosphere as short wave solar radiation and Escape the Earth as long-wave terrestrial radiation. The balance between incoming solar radiation and outgoing terrestrial radiation is known as Heat Budget – Energy Balance.

  • Long-wave terrestrial radiation plays a major role in keeping the atmosphere warm. The atmosphere is warmed primarily by the difference between incoming solar radiation and outgoing terrestrial radiation. This warmth is captured by gases like carbon dioxide leading to the green house effect and global warming.

Atmosphere is heated mostly indirectly: Earth absorbs short-wave solar energy and gives out long-wave radiation, absorbed by carbon dioxide and greenhouse gases; A and R true, R explains A.

Key facts from the book (10 points)
  • A cyclone is a large scale wether system in which winds rotate around a strong center of low atmospheric pressure. Cyclones rotate anticlockwise in the northern hemisphere and clockwise in the southern hemisphere.

  • (1) Tropical Cyclones – (Between tropics of Cancer and Capricorn). Tropical cyclones are known by different names in different places. In northern and Northwestern part of Australia they are called Willy-Willy, in China, they are called typhoons, in the USA they are known as hurricanes and in India they are called cyclones. In the Great Plains of USA, strong cyclones are formed as a result of Cold polar winds coming in the contact with hot air brought by Gulf streams. These cyclones are called tornadoes. Tornado Alley is the name given to the region of the Great Plains affected by Tornados. The places located in the Tornado Alley are – Mississippi-Missouri Valley, Texas, Oklahoma, Kansas and Nebraska. Tornados are common in the entire tropical and subtropical region but are very prominent in the Caribbean Sea and North America Region.
  • Fujita scale is used to measure the intensity of tornadoes.
  • Hurricane is a tropical cyclone affecting the regions of Texas, Mexico, Florida and West Indies. Saffir Simpson scale is used to measure potential property damage caused by a hurricane.
  • Typhoon is also a tropical cyclone that originates in the South China Sea. Nargis was a tropical cyclone responsible for heavy destruction in Myanmar.

(2) Temperate Cyclones – These cyclones originate in the mid latitudes.They are often round, building or wedge-shaped. These cyclones are found between 35°-65° latitudes in both hemispheres. Under the influence of the westerlies blow from west to east.

  • Anticyclones have high pressure at their center, around which air circulates.
  • The pressure decreases from centre towards the outer periphery due to which air blows from the center outwards.
  • Anticyclones are clockwise in the northern hemisphere and anticlockwise in the southern hemisphere.

  • The water vapor present in the atmosphere is known as humidity. Humidity is a result of evaporation of water from the earth surface which reaches the atmosphere. Humidity is expressed in two ways –

Key facts from the book (10 points)

∗Air occupies space and has weight. The atmosphere exerts vertical pressure on the earth’s surface. This is called atmospheric pressure.

  • Atmospheric pressure is measured using a barometer. It is measured, as the force exerted per unit area of the barometer. A sudden fall in the level of barometer is a sign of an upcoming storm.   • A continuous rise in the level of mercury in the barometer is a sign of an anticyclone and clear weather.
  • The horizontal distribution of atmospheric pressure is shown by using isobars.
  • An isobar is an imaginary line that connects points having same atmospheric pressure at mean sea level. ∗Based on the process of origin, pressure belts can be divided into two parts-

(1) Based on thermogenesis – pressure belts thus formed are equatorial low-pressure belts and polar high-pressure belts.

(2) Based on motion-pressure belts thus formed are sub tropical high-pressure belts and sub-polar low-pressure belts. ∗Equatorial Low-Pressure Belts – The belt extends between 5° north and south of Equator. The equator receives vertical rays of the sun throughout the year. As a result, the air gets heated and starts rising up. Hence the region always experiences low pressure. The surface air of the region moves with very slow velocity as a result of which the environment here is quite calm. This is the reason this pressure belt is also called Doldrums.

  • Sub-tropical High-Pressure Belt – the belt is found between 30°-35° latitudes in both hemispheres. The air rising from the equator starts becoming cooler in the upper layers of atmosphere and hence begins sinking near 30°-35° latitudes. Simultaneously the air from the sub-polar low-pressure belts also starts descending in this region due to Earth's rotation thus a high-pressure zone is created which gives birth to sub tropical high pressure belt. The pressure belt is highly mobile in nature, thus it is also called Horse Latitude.
  • Sub-Polar Low-Pressure Belt – This pressure belt is found between 60°-65° latitudes in both hemispheres. Though the temperature in this region is low throughout the year the region experiences low pressure. This is due to the fact that rotation of the Earth causes the air to spread and displaces it. As a result low pressure is created.
  • Polar High-Pressure Belts – The poles and the regions in close proximity to them experience high pressure because the region is very cold which causes the air to become heavy and start descending creating high pressure.

Sub-polar low-pressure belt lies at 60°-65° latitude in both hemispheres; low-pressure areas are steadier over oceans; both true, but R does not explain A.

Chapter 148

Clouds

7 facts · 0 Must know

Test mode is on: tap a grey box to reveal the answer.

Key facts from the book (9 points)

∗ Cloud is a visible dense mass of water droplets or ice crystals suspended in the atmosphere. Hence, collectively clouds are a large version of suspended water bodies or glacial bodies. Clouds are found at a relatively higher altitude compared to fog.

∗Clouds can be categorized depending on their shape, vertical expansion and height.

Cirrus–Clouds – They clouds are found at the highest altitude. These are fibrous and feathery in appearance as they are made up of tiny ice crystals. When the rays of the sun pass through these ice crystals the cirrus clouds appear white in colour. They are seen before the advent of a cyclone. Cirro–Stratus Cloud – They are found at an altitude of 18000 feet and above. Their arrival creates a halo around the Sun and the Moon which is a sign of an upcoming cyclone. Cirro-Cumulus Clouds – These clouds are white in appearance and are found in clusters of small ball-shaped patches.

Alto-Stratus Clouds – These are those high clouds that are spread across the sky as thin sheets of blue and brown clouds. They are responsible for continuous and expanded rainfall. Alto – Cumulus Clouds – They are low-level clouds just like cirro-cumulus clouds.

Strato-Cumulus-Clouds – These are light brown coloured clouds often found in big round shaped patches.

Stratus Clouds – They are formed as a result of two opposite air bodies, coming into contact with each other. They are often seen during winter in temperate regions.

Nimbo-Stratus Clouds – They are found close to the surface of the Earth. These grey, often dark clouds are highly dense in nature and can be of any shape. It is because of their highly dense nature that they block the sunlight and make the region dark followed by heavy rainfall.

Cumulus Clouds – They are highly dense in nature. Their shape is elongated and the upper portion of them resembles a dome or a cauliflower. These clouds are a signal of the start of clear weather.

Cumulo-Nimbus-Clouds – These clouds are highly diversified and dense in nature. There is a high possibility of rain, hail and thunderstorms associated with these clouds. ∗Thunder is a process of a thunderstorm. In reality, thunderstorms are local storms in which the air ascends with high velocity. Lightning and thunder is witnessed followed by heavy rainfall. Lightning causes a sudden and high increase in the temperature of the air leading to a sudden expansion in the air which result in thunder.

Clouds → condensation of water vapour into tiny water droplets or ice crystals.

Chapter 149

The Winds

12 facts · 0 Must know

Test mode is on: tap a grey box to reveal the answer.

Key facts from the book (11 points)
  • The movement of air as a result of the difference in horizontal air pressure is known as wind. Wind in general flows from a high- pressure area to a low-pressure area. If the earth were still and flat, the winds would blow from a high-pressure area directly to a low-pressure area along the isobaric lines at an angle of 90o. However, the Earth is geoid in shape and rotates on its own axis. Hence winds under the influence of dynamic forces keep shifting their trajectory. Types of Winds – There are basically three types of wind Planetary Winds – Winds blowing constantly in a particular direction throughout the year are called planetary winds. The main planetary winds are – trade winds, westerlies and polar easterlies.
  • Trade winds are winds blowing from sub tropical high-pressure belts toward equatorial low-pressure belts in both the hemispheres.
  • Westerlies- They blow from sub-tropical high-pressure belts (30°-35°) toward sub-polar low-pressure belts (60°-65°) in both the hemisphere. Since there is more landmass in Northern Hemisphere compared to Southern Hemisphere the westerlies in the former case are more complex, and they are less influential in summers as compared to winter.
  • Due to the presence of less landmass in the Southern Hemisphere the westerlies travel at such a high speed causes them to become stormy. It is because of this high intensity of the westerlies in the southern hemisphere that around 40° latitudes they are known as Roaring Forties, around 50° latitude they are called Furious Fifties and around 60° latitude they are called Shrieking Sixties.
  • Wellington (New Zealand) is the only capital in the world that lies in the path of Roaring Forties.
  • Polar winds blow from polar high-pressure belt to sub-polar low-pressure belt.

Periodic winds – Winds are those that reverse their direction as per season or time. The important periodic winds are – monsoonal winds, land and sea breezes, breezes of mountains and valleys. Monsoonal winds are those that completely reverse their direction according to seasons. During the six months of summer they blow from sea to land and during the six month of winter they blow from land to sea.

  • Land and Sea Breezes only cover 20 to 30 km of the area including the coastal area. During daytime the land heats up faster than the nearby sea as a result low pressure is created over land and thus cool and moist winds blow from sea to land. This wind is called a sea breeze. There is a complete reversal in the direction of the wind during the night. As a result, winds blow from land to sea. This wind is called Land breeze.
  • Mountain and Valley Breeze - During daytime the air heats up and rises along the slope of the mountain. This is known as Valley Breeze (Anabatic flow). During the night the air gets cooler and heavier as a result it starts descending along the slope of the mountain. This is known as Mountain Breeze (Katabatic flow).

(3) Local Winds – These winds are generated as a result of regional differences in temperature or air pressure. Hence, they affect a very small area.

∗The Mediterranean Sea is located between 30° to 40° North Latitudes. Hence, the sea comes under the influence of the sub-tropical high-pressure belt. This belt is mobile in nature. During summers, the trade winds blow in these latitudes and in winter these latitudes come under the influence of westerlies. This means that the westerlies blow towards North east from this region and Trade Winds blow towards south west from this region.

Coriolis force → increases with wind speed; maximum at the poles, absent at the Equator; deflects winds right in the north, left in the south.

Chapter 150

The Local Winds

9 facts · 1 Must know

Test mode is on: tap a grey box to reveal the answer.

Key facts from the book (16 points)
  • Local winds are generated as a result of pressure and temperature gradient in a particular region and hence affect a very small area. These winds are confined to the lower level of the troposphere.

Important local winds are as Follows:

  • Chinook means snow-eater. These winds descend along the eastern slope of the Rocky Mountains and are warm and dry in nature. These winds increase the temperature of the region during winters resulting in the melting of snow and the emergence of fresh greenery in the region. The winds rising along the southern slope of Alps descend along the northern slope and are warm and dry in nature. It is called Foehn in Europe and has its maximum influence in Switzerland.
  • Santa Ana is a local wind prevailing in Southern California. It is also a warm and dry wind like Chinook but unlike Chinook, it blows as a Channel Wind in the valley east to west.
  • Harmattan is a local wind that blows in a northeast and east direction in the western parts of Sahara Desert. It is also dry and dusty air. With the advent of Harmattan, the weather becomes dry, pleasant and healthy. It is the reason why Harmattan is also called Doctor Wind in the coastal areas of Guinea.
  • Sirocco is a local wind that blows from the Sahara Desert towards the Mediterranean Sea. The wind is dry, warm and sandy in nature. This air contains a lot of red sand. When blowing over the Mediterranean Sea the wind absorbs moisture and occasionally provides the southern Italy region with rainfall. When red particles descends along with rain it is known as Blood Rain. The sand carried by Sirocco from Libya is transported to Malta, Italy, Spain, Croatia, Montenegro, Albania and Greece.
  • Simoom is a local wind that blows in the deserts of Arabia and Kurdistan.
  • Mistral is a cold polar wind that blows around the northwestern part of the Roum Sea, affecting the areas of Spain and France.
  • Bora is a dry cold air that moves at a very fast pace. It prevails along the eastern coasts of Adriatic Sea. The northern part of Italy is highly influenced by Bora.
  • Loo is a dry and hot local wind that prevails in northern India. It blows from northwest and west to the east. These winds are tropical and dry and travel at a high velocity.
  • Norwesters are pre monsoon thunderstorms blowing in India which are also known as Kalbaisakhi.
  • Zonda is a warm dry wind that blows along the eastern slopes of the Andes Mountains and influences the country of Argentina.
  • Black Roller is a local wind prevailing in the Great Plains region of North America.
  • Purga is a cold local wind prevailing in the tundras of Russia.
  • Levanter is a cold local wind that blows from east to west in Spain.
  • Pampero is a local northwestern cold wind of the Pampas region of South America.

Foehn → Alps (Switzerland); Simoom → Arabia and Kurdistan deserts; Santa Ana → southern California; Zonda → Argentina (east Andes). Must know

Chapter 152

The World Climate

42 facts · 7 Must know

Test mode is on: tap a grey box to reveal the answer.

Key facts from the book (17 points)
  • Climate is the average weather in a place over a certain period of time. It is determined by the daily weather conditions of a place (like temperature, rainfall, winds, humidity, air pressure etc) persisting over a long duration of time.
  • Earth has been basically divided into three climatic zones – Tropical Zone, Temperate Zone and Frigid Zone. These zones extend from the equatorial region towards poles.
  • The continent of Asia extends from equatorial region to North Pole. As a result, all types of climates are found here. Different climates are found in different parts of the world. Places having same climates are called climatic regions and they are as follows:
  • Equatorial Climatic Region – Found in between 0° to 10° North and South of the equator. The temperature remains high in this region all throughout the year. As a result, the region remains humid and it receives rainfall in the afternoon. The flora of the region consists of broadleaf evergreen trees like Gutta Percha, Rubber, Ebony, Palm, Bamboo, Bet, Mahogany, Sandal, Cinchona, etc. The regions under this climate include

– Amazon Basin, the Congo Basin of Africa, Guinea Coast, Eastern island groups, and eastern Central American (Panama, Costa Rica, Nicaragua, Honduras, Guatemala).

  • Tropical Monsoonal Climatic Region – The region lies in the route of trade winds. Places included in this region are – India, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Thailand, Cambodia, Laos, Eastern Coastal Regions of Africa, South-Eastern coastal parts of USA and northern parts of Australia etc.
  • Sahara Type of Climatic Region – Also known as a tropical dry desert type of climate. The climate extends between 15° to 30° latitudes on both sides of the equator in the western parts of the continent. There are two distinct seasons in this type of climate, the summer season and the winter season. Seasons are distinguished based on temperature. The average temperature of the summers is between 30°-35°C. According to the readings of NASA’s satellite (2003-2009) Dasht-e-Lut desert of Iran was the hottest place on the planet based on surface temperature. Highest recorded temperature in 2005 was 70.7°C. Places under Sahara type of climate includes – Thar desert and Arabian Peninsula of Asia, Sahara and Kalahari deserts of Africa, Western deserts of Australia, Atacama desert of South America and Western desert of North America.
  • Savanna type of climatic region – the temperature of the equatorial type of climate and savanna type of climate are some what the same. Since the savanna type of climate lies between the equatorial type of climate and tropical desert climate, the region is dominated by grasslands. The savanna type of climate is also called Sudan type of climate. There is a distinct dry and moist season however the temperature is high throughout the year. The places included in this region are – Venezuela, Colombia, Guyana, South-Central Brazil, and Paraguay. The maximum extent of savanna type of climate in Africa is found in Sudan and northern region of Australia.
  • Mediterrannean Type of Climatic Region: Also known as sub-tropical dry summer type of climate. Since this type of climate is found near the Mediterranean Sea it is known as Mediterranean Climate. Mediterranean type of climate is found between 30° to 40° latitudes in both the hemispheres on the western parts of the continents. Maximum rainfall occurs in winter. Summers are dry and winters are wet. The summer winds are dry in nature. The places included under the Mediterranean type of climate are – river valleys of France, southern Italy, Greece, western Turkiye, western Israel, and North Western Africa which includes Algeria, Southern California of North America, Central Chile, and south-western part of South Africa.
  • Steppe Type of Climate – This type of climate is found in the temperate grassland regions. This type of climate is found in the middle latitudes in the central parts of the continent. The annual range of temperature is high and annual rainfall is between 250 to 750 milimeter. Places included in steppe type of climate are – grasslands of USA and Canada, grasslands of South Australia and Eurasia.
  • Western European Climate – Found between 40° to 65° latitudes in both the hemispheres in the western part of the continents. The average temperature is between 15°-21°C. There is a good amount of rainfall in this climate however rainfall increases in winter as compared to summer. Places included in Western European type of climate are – North Western Europe, Western Norway, Denmark, North Western Germany, France, Oregon and Washington in the USA, British Columbia in Canada, Chile and New Zealand.
  • St. Lawrence Type of Climate – It is a moist continental type of climate, found on the eastern ends of the continent, predominantly in the Northern Hemisphere between 45° to 65° latitudes. There is a good amount of rainfall throughout the year but more in summer as compared to winter. The places included under St. Lawrence type of climate are – Manchuria region of China, St. Lawrence Valley of North America and the coastal provinces of Canada.
  • •Taiga Type of Climate – Also known as a Siberian type of climate which comes under microthermal climate. The winters are long and the summers are of short duration. The 10°C temperature the warmest month of a region determines the Northern limit of Taiga. Winter season is approximately 8 months long during which the temperature remains well below freezing point.
  • Beyond the Polar regions lowest temperature was recorded in Greenland – 69.6°C (-93.3°F) in December, 1991.
  • The lowest temperature in the world was recorded in Vostok in Eastern Antarctica on 21st July, 1983, which was –

89.2°C (-128.6°F). The average annual rainfall in Taiga type of climate is between 370 to 600 millimeters, however, maximum rainfall is in the form of snow. Places included in this type of climate are Alaska of USA, Northernmost parts of Canada, from Scandinavia in the west to Siberia in the east, in Eurasia.

  • Tundra Type of Climate – It has the least vegetation and is found in Polar and Arctic regions. The ecological productivity is minimal. In tundra type of climate, there is a deficiency in solar heat as a result the temperature remains very low throughout the year. The annual average rainfall is less than 400 mm. Tundras extend from the southern limits of northern glaciers to southern limits of Taiga in the South, and include the regions of America and Eurasia. Tundra only supports limited flora such as Lichens and Moss Flora that can tolerate cold polar climate for example, those of high mountains, Alpines and tundra region are called hekistotherms.

Seasonal change in day and night length comes from Earth's revolution around the Sun on a tilted axis; without the tilt, days and nights would be equal everywhere.

Chapter 153

The Soil

16 facts · 0 Must know

Test mode is on: tap a grey box to reveal the answer.

Key facts from the book (23 points)
  • ∗Soils are formed as a result of disintegration and decomposition of loosened and unorganized rock materials, fossils of flora and fauna, water and air. Bedrock, climatic and biotic factors play a vital role in the formation of soil. The color, formation and minerals of the soil depend upon the bedrock.
  • Earthworms contribute to the formation of the soil and also increase its productivity. Hence, they are known as engineers of the ecosystem. Earthworms create pores in the soil, allowing the percolation of air and water and release of carbon dioxide.
  • The faeces of earthworms are helpful in increasing the productivity of the soil. Earthworms soften the soil. They act as decomposers for the soil.
  • The excreted urea and dead matter of living organisms (flora and fauna) are decomposed by decomposers in the soil.
  • This maintains the nitrogen cycle and keeps providing nitrogen to the soil.
  • Soil profile is a vertical section of soil in which all the soil horizons are shown. They are as follows:

(1) Eluviations – The matter of upper stratum descends downwards.

(2) Illuviation – Different salts are introduced from the upper horizon to lower due to percolation of water.

(3) Capillary Action – It is responsible for upward movement of water from wet areas to dry areas of the soil. The smaller the pore the higher the capillary action and vice versa.

  • The capillary function is highest clay soil and lowest in sandy soils. The effectiveness of capillary action in four different soils is as follows – Clay > Loam > Sandy soil > Sand. Podzol is a light colored soil of wood regions, mostly found in a cold temperate climate.
  • Chernozem soil is found in grassland and transitional areas. It is mostly found in a temperate steppe climate and is also found in humid grasslands.
  • Laterite soil is found in warm moist areas. The top layer of this soil has oxides of iron and salts of aluminum present.
  • Chestnut soil is found in dry areas. It is dark brown in color and has a low humus content compared to Chernozem soil.
  • Sierozem soil is found in deserts of mid-latitudes.
  • Terra Rossa soil is a reddish silty soil, formed as a result of weathering of limestones and dolomites.
  • Prairie soil is found in the grassland areas of temperate regions. The soil is a mixture of Chernozem soil and greyish Podzol soil.
  • Soil conservation is not only about protecting the soil from erosion but also about taking measures to conserve soil fertility. To be precise sustainable use of soil is known as soil conservation.
  • Soil erosion is a process through which the top layer of soil along with nutrients is eroded from one place to another.
  • Contour Bunding is a method used to conserve soil in hilly areas. During rainfall, it prevents the soil from washing away. Under Contour Banding terrace like structures are made on the slopes of the hilly areas which prevent the soil from washing away with the downfllow of water.
  • Since the tropical forests receive rain throughout the year the soils of the region are suffering from leaching.
  • Halophytes are vegetation that grow well in saline soil.
  • Vegetations growing well in cold regions is called Cryophytes.
  • Vegetation growing well in rock terrain are called Lithophytes, vegetation growing well in tropical deserts are called Xerophytes and vegetation growing well in swamps and marshes is called Hygrophytes. Hydrophytes are aquatic plants.

Correct order of agricultural practices → Soil preparation → Sowing → Irrigation → Harvesting.

Chapter 154

The Major Tribes of the World

37 facts · 4 Must know

Test mode is on: tap a grey box to reveal the answer.

Key facts from the book (31 points)
  • Tribal peoples are those groups of people who are similar to each other on the basis of social customs, language and culture.
  • Nomadic Tribes are those groups of people that travel from one place to another to find fodder for their cattle. Though nomadic tribes are found all over the world, they are mostly concentrated in arid regions. They are primarily found in the arid regions of Africa, Central Asia, and South America.
  • When people shift from one location to another in a particular season and then return to the same location after that season is over, it is called seasonal migration For example when it starts to snow in the mountains the tribal people shift to the valley and return after the winter season is over.
  • Gaddi, Bakarwal and Bhotia are some of the tribes of India that practice seasonal migration.
  • Pygmy Tribe is found in the rainforests of Congo Basin in Equatorial Africa. They are hunters and gatherers. They construct huts at the tops of trees which are called Mongulu. They are black short- statured people of Negrito race.
  • Eskimo tribes are found in the tundra regions of Alaska, Canada and Greenland. They are of Mongoloid race and hunting is their main occupation. They use a weapon called the harpoon and a Yayak boat to catch fish.
  • Inuit is a cultural group of indigenous people found in Arctic regions of Canada, Greenland (Denmark), Russia and Alaska.
  • Maasai tribes are found in the plateau regions of East Africa which include Kenya, northern Tanzania and eastern Uganda. They are cattle herders and their main occupation is cattle rearing. They live in huts called Kraal.
  • Bushman Tribe is found in desert regions of Kalahari which include South Africa, Zimbabwe, Eswatini, Botswana, Namibia, etc Hunting and gathering is their main occupation. They are omnivorous. Termites are called the rice of Bushman.
  • Zulu tribes reside in South Africa. They are known for their culture and rituals. The Battle of Isandlwana was fought between the British and Zulu tribe in 1879. The tribe practices agriculture and cattle rearing.
  • Semang tribe resides on the island of Malay in Malaysia. They belong to Negrito race and depend on hunting and gathering.
  • Sakai tribe is found in the forests of the Malay Peninsula, Malaysia and Indonesia. They use blowpipes for hunting.
  • Papua tribes reside in Papua New Guinea (Pacific Ocean). They practice agriculture and cattle rearing.
  • The Sami tribe (Lapps tribe) is found in Norway, Sweden, Finland and the Kola Peninsula in Russia. The region is also known as Fenno Scandinavia.
  • Bedouin tribes are found in the desert regions of Arabia, especially in the northern part of Saudi Arabia. Living in tribal groups they practice a migratory lifestyle. They belong to Armenoids and Mediterranean (Caucasian) races.
  • The Bora tribe is found in the coastal areas of Western Amazon Basin, Brazil, Peru and Colombia. They practice primitive agriculture and are known to be cruel in nature.
  • Kirghiz tribe is a group in Central Asia spread between Pamir Plateau in Kyrgyzstan and the Tianshan mountain range. Kirghiz tribes are cattle rearing tribes that practice seasonal migration. They build round shaped temporary tents known as Yurts.
  • Yupik tribe is found in Eastern Russia and Western Alaska. The tribe uses sledges (ice carts driven by dogs).
  • Yukaghir is a Mongoloid tribe found in Verkhoyansk (North-East Siberia) and Stanovoy Mountains.
  • Maya tribe is found in Central America, mainly in Mexico, Guatemala and Honduras.
  • Maori is a Polynesian tribe residing in New Zealand. Their main occupation is agriculture and gathering.
  • Among the other tribes of the world – Fulani tribes reside in West Africa, Bantu tribe resides in eastern, southern and central Africa, Nuba tribe resides in Sudan, Vedda tribe is found in Sri Lanka, Barber tribe resides in Morocco and north Africa Enu tribe resides in Japan and Aeta tribe is found in the Philippines.
  • Important tribes of India are – Oran, Gond, Kol, Santhal, Bheel and Toda.
  • India is believed to be the indigenous place of the Gypsy. The Gypsy people are believed to be associated with dome Caste (Scheduled Caste) of India.
  • Archaeopteryx was the first bird to emerge on Earth somewhere around 150 million years ago.
  • Africa is believed to be the birthplace of Mankind. At present, Caucasian race is counted amongthe largest races on Earth. They have straight or curly hairs, dark blue or brown eyes and a cranial Index of80 and above. Hobble and Elliot Smith have categorized Caucasians in to three groups
  • – Nordic, Alpine and Mediterranean.
  • Caucasians are the largest group in the world.
  • Mongoloid race is mostly found in Central and Eastern Asia. They have yellowish and brown skin and a small forehead.
  • Negroids are dark brown to brown in appearance. Africa is their indigenous place.
  • Cro-Magnon is believed to be the most modern of the human species. It existed up to the emergence of the present modern man i.e. Homo sapiens. The first evidence of Cro-Magnon was found in an excavation in France in Dordogne Valley in 1868. It is believed that Cro Magnon dates from the Upper Paleolithic Period (40000 to 10000 years ago).

Economic Geography

100 facts · 7 Must know

Key facts from the book (41 points)

A. Agriculture & Livestock

  • Grains are the main source of food for humankind. The important grains are Rice, Wheat, Corn, Millet, Barley, Chickpea, and Pulses etc.
  • Rice is cultivated in tropical, semitropical and temperate regions. Hence rice is grown in most of the wet humid areas of the world, although it can be grown in arid regions also with the help of irrigation. In most areas around the world, rice is grown as a Kharif crop, which is harvested in Nov.-Dec., but in Java, it is harvested in April-May. The International Rice Gene Bank, maintained by International Rice Research Institute (IRRI) is located in Los Banos (Philippines). IRRI was established in the year 1960. Paddy is very famous in China. Out of the total area under rice cultivation in China halfis used to cultivate hybrid rice.
  • According to FAO, 2024 India has the maximum area under rice cultivation (50.51 million hectare) followed by China (29.26 million hectare). Despite having less area under rice cultivation, China has a total area under irrigation whereas in India only half of the area under rice cultivation is irrigated. According to Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) 2024 the four leading producers of rice in the world are - 1. India (217.87 million tonnes), 2. China (207.53 million tonnes), 3. Bangladesh (60.57 million tonnes), 4. Indonesia (53.14 million tonnes) and 5. Vietnam (43.45 million tonnes).
  • According to latest updates – from FAO 2024, Tajikistan has the largest productivity of rice (13385.8 kg/ha) followed by Australia (11914.4 kg/ha).
  • Wheat is basically a temperate crop. Its cultivation spreads up to 60° latitudes in Northern Hemisphere and up to 40° latitudes in Southern Hemisphere. Wheat requires an average temperature of 10°C during germination and an average temperature between 15°-20°C during the development of grains. A Timely rainfall between 20 cm and 70 cm is also required.
  • According to FAO, 2024 the top four leading producers of wheat in the world are – China (140.10 million tonnes), India (113.29 million tonnes), Russia (82.59 million tonnes) and the USA (53.65 million tonnes).
  • Sugarcane requires a tropical as well as subtropical climate where the average temperature is between 21°C-27°C with average rainfall between 75 cm 150 cm. According to FAO 2024, the top five leading producers of sugarcane in the world are – 1. Brazil (759.66 million tonnes), 2. India (453.16 million tonnes), 3. China (102.09 million tonnes), 4. Pakistan (84.24 million tonnes), 5. Thailand (82.44 million tonnes).
  • Sugar beet is a plant of temperate climate.According to FAO 2024 the two largest producers of sugar beet in the world are Russia and the Germany. Russia and the Germany are followed by France, USA and Turkiye. In Ukraine, the entire production of sugar is from sugar beet.
  • Cotton is a tropical and subtropical plant. Quality and type of cotton are determined by the length of the fibers, shine, etc. According to FAO 2023 the top 5 leading producers of cottonseed in the world are – 1. India (10.60 million tonnes), 2. China (9.40 million tonnes), 3. Brazil (4.49 million tonnes), 4. USA (3.31 million tonnes), 5. Pakistan (3.17 million tonnes), while the top 5 leading producers in terms of cotton lint are (FAO 2023)

– 1. China (5.62 million tonnes), 2. India (5.53 million tonnes),

3. Brazil (2.92 million tonnes) 4. USA (2.63 million tonnes),

  • 5. Pakistan (1.74 million tonnes).

  • 1.59 million tonnes of castor oilseeds. India is followed by Mozambique (0.07 million tonnes), Brazil (0.03 million tonnes).
  • According to FAO 2024, the top 5 leading producers of bananas in the world are – India (37.61 million tonnes), China (11.76 million tonnes), Indonesia (9.26 million tonnes), Ecuador (7.56 million tonnes) and Brazil (7.05 million tonnes).
  • According to FAO 2024, the top 4 leading producers of coconut (shell) in the world are – 1. Indonesia (17.99 million tonnes), 2. India (14.71 million tonnes), 3. Philippines (14.50 million tonnes) and 4. Brazil (3.16 million tonnes).
  • Tobacco cultivation requires high temperatures. It grows well between 21° to 27°C. Tobacco requires an annual average rainfall of100 to 120 centimeters. According to FAO 2024, the leading producers of tobacco (unmanufacture) in the world are – (1) China (2.26 million tonnes), (2) India (0.73 million tonnes), (3) Brazil (0.64 million tonnes), (4) Indonesia (0.53 million tonnes) and (5) Zimbabwe (0.24 million tonnes).
  • Rubber is obtained from the latex of a tree found in the equatorial evergreen forests. Cote d'Ivoire (1686.59 thousand tonnes),

(2) Coffea Robusta – Grown on a large scale in Africa, in countries such as Ethiopia and Uganda. Colombia (839.85 thousand tonnes), 4. Indonesia (807.58 thousand tonnes), 5. Ethiopia (575.69 thousand tonnes), 6. Uganda (402.00 thousand tonnes), 7. India (363.00 thousand tonnes).
  • Tea is a plant of the tropical and subtropical regions but can also be grown in the hilly areas of the temperate zones. Tea requires a long summer with an average temperature between 20°-30°C. Tea also requires average rainfall between 130 and 150 cm.
  • According to FAO 2024 China produces the maximum tea leaves (16260.90 thousand tonnes) in the world followed by India (6156.03 thousand tonnes), Kenya (2687.20 thousand tonnes), Sri Lanka (1514.02 thousand tonnes) and Turkiye (1414.00 thousand tonnes).

Argentina (57494.50 thousand tonnes), 5. India (40230.57 thousand tonnes).

However according to Ministry of Commerce and Industry plantation crops include – Tea, Coffee, Rubber and Spices. Hence, plantation agriculture includes – Coconut, Arecanut, Cocoa, Cashew nut, Tea, Coffee, Rubber and Spices.
  • Horticulture includes Pomology (Cultivation of Fruits), Olericulture (cultivation of Vegetables) and Floriculture (Cultivation of Flowers). Now, Mushrooms, Bamboo, Spices etc. have also been brought under the definition of Horticulture. Horticulture requires a lot of manual labor. Coffee cultivation is a horticultural practice in Hawaii (USA). The coffee of Hawaii is famously known as Kona coffee. Mocha coffee is produced in Yemen. Mocha is the name of the harbor from where it is imported.
  • The diverse climate of India ensures the production of a variety of vegetables and fruits. According to FAO, 2024 India is the largest producer of fruit (other fruit, n.e.c.), and second largest producer of vegetables (other vegetables, fresh n.e.c.) after China.

  • Taungya is a type of shifting agriculture practised in Myanmar. Chena, jhuming and milpa are also associated with shifting agriculture.
  • The regions of Europe close to the Mediterranean Sea are famous for the cultivation of grapes. Around 85% of the total grapes produced are used for making wines.
  • Sacramento-San Joaquin Valley is located in California (USA). Sacramento is a flat/internal valley, the where River San Joaquin creates an inland delta. The valley is world famous for grapes and citrus fruit.
  • Golden Crescent is the name given to the countries that produce and export poppy. Countries included in the Golden Crescent are Pakistan, Iran and Afghanistan.
  • Groundnuts are native to Brazil, Mato Grosso and its nearby areas. Groundnut is the main crop of Gambia and has a major role to play in the country’s GDP (Gross Domestic Product). First time in the world, American agronomist Norman Borlaug developed the high yielding variety (HYV) seeds in Mexico. According to the International Agreement on Agriculture, a Green Box is an instrument through which economic assistance is provided in the fields of– research related to control of insects and disease, training, general awareness, marketing and promotion activities.
  • Shahtoosh is a special woolen shawl made out of the hairs of Tibetan Antelope and Chiru. Chiru is found in the Chinese Autonomous Region of Tibet. Earlier it was also found in western Nepal. Chiru is also found in the union territory of Ladakh. Apiculture is associated with the rearing of honey bees for honey production.
  • Viticulture is associated with study and production of grapes.
  • According to FAO, 2023 China is the largest producer of raw silk in the world, followed by India. Other countries producing silk include Uzbekistan, Vietnam, Democratic People's Republic of Korea and Brazil.
  • Nitrogen is an essential element for the development of plants. It is important for the development of plant cells and tissues hence a deficiency of nitrogen hampers the growth of plants causing the leaves to turn yellowish in colour and dry up. Rhizobium, Azotobacter, Azospirillum and blue-green algae are used as bio-fertilizers for crops.
  • Blue-green algae is used as a bio-fertilizer in paddy fields, whereas azotobacter is used as a bio-fertilizer for paddy wheat, maize, mustard, potato, cotton etc. Azospirillum is used as a bio-fertilizer for Paddy, Sorghum, Millet, Sugarcane, Maize etc.
  • Alfa-Alfa is a flowering plant of the Fabaceae pea family. It is cultivated as an important fodder crop. In the United Kingdom, Australia, South Africa and New Zealand, it is called Lucerne grass.
  • Animal husbandry is more developed in those regions where natural grazing lands or grasslands are found in abundance. The credit for commercializing animal husbandry is given to European migrants. Ranches are large farms for cattle grazing. They are built by enclosing natural grasslands with barbed wire and then using them as grazing lands for livestock. Maximum livestocks is found in Asia. According to FAO 2020, the countries with maximum livestock population are – China (829.58 million), India (545.33 million), Brazil (304.15 million), and USA (201.69 million). Chapter 157

The Minerals

15 facts · 1 Must know

Test mode is on: tap a grey box to reveal the answer.

Key facts from the book (10 points)

(i) Coal

  • When small pieces of rock collect below the surface, it leads to the formation of sedimentary rock also known as layered rocks. Fossils and fossil fuels are found in the sedimentary rocks. Sedimentary rocks occupy 75% of the total Earth's surface.
  • Minerals such as coal, slate, marble, salt (rock), petroleum are found in sedimentary rocks. Coal and limestone are examples of sedimentary rocks ofbiotic origin.
  • Based on the percentage of carbon present coal is categorized into four types–(1) Anthracite - It is the best quality of coal having a carbon content of 90%–95%. (2) Bituminous – It is next to Anthracite in terms of quality having a carbon content of 70% to 90%. (3) Lignite - Famously known as brown coal having a carbon content of 45%–50%. It is mostly used in thermal power plants. (4) Peat –It is low-grade coal having a carbon content of 40% or less. Rock coal is also known as Anthracite. It is the highest quality of coal.
  • According to data from World Mineral Production 2019-2023 in the year 2023, China produced more than half of the world's production of coal. The top three leading producers (2022) of coal in the world are – (1) China, (2) India, (3) Indonesia. The top 5 countries in terms reserves of coal in the world by the end of year 2023 are USA, Russia, China, Australia and India respectively.
  • The North Appalachian coal area is the largest coal area in the USA. The region produces the best quality of coal. The other important coal regions of USA are – South Appalachian, Western Interior coal region and the coal region of Rocky Mountains etc.
  • Ruhr is a river that flows through Germany. The Ruhr Valley is the main coal region and industrial area known as Ruhr Basin.
  • Saarland is located on the borders of France and Germany in the Saar River valley. This area is said to have huge deposits of coal.
  • Donets Basin, also known as Donbass is currently located in Ukraine. It is an important coal producing region.
  • Provinces of Shaanxi and Sichuan in China are important coal producing areas. Kuznets Basin of Russia and Lancashire in the U.K. are also famous for coal production.

Coal → sedimentary rock (layered; holds fossils and mineral oil). Coal grades: anthracite (90-95% carbon) > bituminous (most abundant) > lignite (brown coal) > peat.

1 paper question

Coal, crude oil and natural gas → fossil fuels, formed over millions of years from remains of living organisms.

Key facts from the book (9 points)
  • Copper is the most important metal after Iron in the field of industries.
  • Huge reserves of copper are found on the western slope of Andes Mountains, ranging from northern Peru to central Chile.
  • According to World Mineral Production 2019- 23 in the year 2023 Chile is the largest producer of copper ore.
  • Huge deposits of porphyry copper are found in the mountainous region of Andes. The Chuquicamata copper mine in northern Chile is located in this region. These copper deposits are believed to be of post Eocene, Oligocene epoch. Copper was first produced in the USA in the Keweenaw Peninsula of the state of Michigan. Apart from this copper was also produced in the Butte region of Montana in the USA.
  • The largest copper producing area of Canada is Sudbury (Ontario). Also, the Canadian regions of Flin Flon and Britannia Beach are famous for copper production. Katanga province of Democratic Republic of the Congo is known for copper mining. It is located near the border of Zambia.
  • Zambia is a landlocked country in Africa. There is a long copper (reserve) belt from Zambia to Katanga (D. R. Congo). Though this belt has large deposits of copper, the lack of marine transport dilutes the possibilities of trading and export of the region's copper.
  • Japan is self-sufficient in copper production. The production of copper in Japan is more than its consumption.

The top Five leading countries in terms of copper reserves are – Chile, Australia, Peru, Russia/Congo, and Mexico.

  • According to the figures of World Mineral Production 2019- 23 the top five leading countries in terms of copper production (in 2023) are–(1) Chile, (2) Democratic Republic of the Congo (3) Peru (4) China and (5) USA.

Petroleum is a liquid, formed as a result of different mixtures ofhydrocarbons. Petroleum is a multicolored substance. The multicolours are due to the mixture of different chemicals present in it. According to Indian Minerals Year Book 2022, the largest share of reserves of world crude oil is available in Middle East (48.3%), followed by South & Central America (18.7%), North America (14%), CIS (8.4%), Africa (7.2%), Asia Pacific (2.6%) and Europe (0.8%).

Large scale production of petroleum is done in Brazil and Colombia. Normally mineral oil is found in those places where other fossil fuels are found. It is also found independently in some places.

  • The highways are better developed and proliferated in developed countries as compared to developing countries.

  • China is a large country whose important cities are connected via road networks. The main highway of Russia connects its capital Moscow to Irkutsk city of the Siberian region.
  • The Capital of Egypt, Cairo is connected to Cape Town in South Africa through an intercontinental highway (Trans-African Highway-4).
  • The Commercial air transport was started by USA in the year 1914, which later proliferated to different parts of the world.
  • There is a dense network of air routes in Western Europe, Eastern USA and southeast Asia. Major air routes are centred in some important places. Among these, some important locations are London, Paris, Rome, Moscow, Karachi, Delhi, Mumbai, Bangkok, Singapore, Tokyo, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Chicago, New York, Rio-de-Janeiro, Karachi, Delhi, Mumbai, etc. The air routes of these places have been arranged according to their respective distances for example, the international flight from Delhi to Tokyo travels on an international route having stoppages at the airports of Bangkok (Thailand), Hanoi (Vietnam), Hong Kong (China) and Taipei City (Taiwan) respectively.
  • Some long-distance air routes of the world are:

(1) Newyork–London–Paris–Rome–Cairo–Delhi–Kolkata– Hongkong–Tokyo route.

(2) New York–San Francisco–Honolulu–Hong Kong– Adelaide–Perth route.

  • Emirates is passenger airline service of United Arab Emirates.
  • The world first public rail transport took place in 1825 between Stockton in Northern England and Darlington.
  • According to World Bank data in terms of total Rail lines in km (in 2021), the top 5 countries are - USA > China > Russia > India > Canada.   • The world’s longest railway route is Trans-Siberian Railway (about 9300 km.). Starting from West of Eurasia in Leningrad, it connects the city of St. Petersburg to Vladivostok which is located in the eastern coast of Pacific Ocean. Note- The main track of Trans-Siberian Railway extends from Vladivostok to Moscow. By using a connecting service it can be traveled to Saint Petersburg in west.
  • Trans Andes is the most important rail route of South America. It connects Valparaiso in Chile to Buenos Aires in Argentina.
  • Orient Express is the most important rail route of Europe. It passes through 8 major countries of Europe. Orient Express connects LC Haure and Paris to the capital of Turkiye i.e. Istanbul. This train operated until 2009.

  • The construction of Canadian Pacific Railway completed in the year 1885.
  • Trans–Australian Railway. It connects originally Port Augusta in South Australia to Kalgoorlie in Western Australia. If latter expanded from Sydney in New South Wales to Perth in Western Australia.
  • Water transport is a relatively inexpensive mode of transport. The important oceanic trade routes of the world are–(1) North Atlantic Ocean route connects the North American industrial region to the industrial regions of Europe. (2) The Mediterranean sea and Indian Ocean route connects the developed regions of Western Europe to developing regions of East Africa, South Asia and East Asia, Via Mediterranean Sea, Red Sea and the Indian Ocean. (3) Suez Canal Route connects the Mediterranean Sea to Red sea. Among all the European countries, Britain has benefited the most from the Suez Canal Route. (4) Cape of Hope route - Prior to the opening of Suez Canal it was the only waterwat option of available. The route made the ships all along the African continent to reach the Red Sea. (5) South Atlantic Route connects the countries of Western Europe and Western Africa to Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay of South America. Some other important sea routes include – North Pacific route, South Pacific route and Panama Canal.
  • Delaware Aqueduct is located in USA. It is the largest rock tunnel in the world. The tunnel is 137 km. long and 13.5 feet to 19.5 feet broad and is used to carry New York city’s water supply. It has been constructed by drilling the hard rocks.

  • Bolmen water tunnel of Sweden is 82 km. long and is used to carry water supply. The Channel Tunnel connects the U.K. and France; it is operated by Eurotunnel.

Chapter 170

The Mapping

6 facts · 0 Must know

Test mode is on: tap a grey box to reveal the answer.

Key facts from the book (8 points)
  • Maps provide us with relevant information regarding regional, territorial and local changes.
  • Isopleth maps provide us information about regions or areas having continuous distribution. Thus isopleths are lines joining places of equal value of quantity, intensity, equal pressure, equal temperature, equal rainfall, equal salinity etc. A very relevant and precise data is required for drawing the lines of isopleths. If there is equitable distribution of the given subject then isopleths become very useful. Moreover, the use of isopleths becomes difficult if the subject is in constant fluctuation for exp. population density.
  • Contours represent elevation topography in comparison to the sea level. It is the most practical and widely used method in showing elevations on a map. When the contours of Isotypes are drawn very close to each other then it signifies steep slopes. Isohypse - isohypse or height contour is a line of equal geopotential height, which are shown on a constant pressure surface. Isogonic lines show the earth’s magnetic declination on a map. Isobaths are imaginary lines, a map that links points at the same depth below the water surface.
  • Isobars are imaginary lines drawn on the maps that links areas having equal air pressure at mean sea level.
  • Isohyets are lines on the map joining areas having an equal amount of rainfall.
  • Isonifs are lines on the mapjoining areas having an equal amount of snowfall.
  • Isohalines are lines on the map joining areas having an equal amount of salinity.
  • Ferdinand Magellan was a Portuguese explorer and the first person to circumnavigate the world.

Daily weather map with isobars → isopleth map (shows continuous data: elevation, rainfall, atmospheric pressure).
